nodes.description: Not a disease-modifying treatment for CMT2T, which has none; supportive orthotic management is curated separately above. Immunoglobulin was given to a homozygous MME patient whose course had acquired demyelinating features on electrophysiology and biopsy, and produced immediate clinical and electrophysiological improvement. It is curated because it identifies a treatable component in a disorder otherwise managed supportively, and because it depends on recognising that not all deterioration in a genotyped patient is genetic. This rests on a single reported patient.

nodes.description: The clinical endpoint: a slowly progressive, relatively mild, distal sensorimotor axonal polyneuropathy with onset typically in the fifth to sixth decade. Patients present with lower-limb weakness, atrophy and sensory disturbance, and unsteady gait. Because onset is late and family history is often absent, the presentation is indistinguishable on clinical grounds from the common acquired axonal neuropathies of the elderly, which is why MME is the leading gene found when those patients are sequenced.

nodes.description: The tissue lesion is axonal degeneration in a length-dependent distribution. Sural nerve from an affected patient shows focally diminished myelinated fibre density, axonal clusters of regenerating axons within single Schwann cells, and skinny axons with redundant myelin loops - the picture of repeated degeneration and regeneration rather than of a primary myelin defect. Electrodiagnostically this is impaired motor and sensory conduction, worse in the lower limbs than the upper.

nodes.description:
This node is where the mechanism stops being known. In peripheral nerve, neprilysin is not distributed uniformly: it is absent from central nervous system myelin but expressed at the inner and outer border of myelinated fibres, in the Schmidt-Lanterman clefts and at the paranodes - the non-compact myelin compartments where Schwann cell and axon exchange signals. Its expression is upregulated in sciatic nerve during the myelination window and downregulated after nerve cut. Those facts make a role in axon-glia signalling plausible.
What is missing is the substrate. Neprilysin hydrolyses enkephalins, substance P, beta-amyloid, gastrin, somatostatin, atrial natriuretic peptide, angiotensin II and endothelin-1 among others, and no study has shown which - if any - accumulates to a damaging level in the nerve of a patient. The authors of the alloimmunisation series state the position plainly: unlike the kidney disease, which is immune mediated and understood, the pathophysiology of the neuropathy is unknown. This node is therefore HYPOTHETICAL and is a placeholder for a mechanism, not a description of one.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion is a loss-of-function variant in MME, present either biallelically or in the heterozygous state. Nonsense, frameshift, splice and missense alleles have all been reported, and they converge functionally rather than structurally: nonsense alleles are degraded by nonsense-mediated decay, a splice variant skips exon 13, and the missense alleles impair catalysis. One recurrent truncating allele, c.466delC (p.Pro156Leufs*14), is shared across four unrelated European families. Transcript levels in lymphocytes were unchanged between patients and controls, so the defect is not detectable as reduced message in an accessible tissue.

genetic_context.description: Germline loss of function. Zygosity is deliberately left unset here because it is the contested variable of this disorder: biallelic in the defining recessive series and in the alloimmunisation families, heterozygous in the dominant cohorts. Setting a single value would encode one side of an unresolved question.

nodes.description: The available mouse model, and its most important result is a negative one. Peripheral nerve morphometry in MME-null mice showed only minor abnormalities in aged animals, far short of the human neuropathy. When the hypothesis that neprilysin has a role in remyelination was tested directly - the hypothesis motivated by neprilysin's localisation to Schmidt-Lanterman clefts and paranodes and by its neuregulin-1-dependent regulation after injury - the knockout was indistinguishable from wild type in axon regeneration, remyelination and functional motor recovery.

The functional consequence, and the step that is best evidenced in patients. Neprilysin protein is absent or reduced in peripheral nerve, tissue availability of the enzyme is strongly decreased, and measured enzymatic activity is significantly impaired. Blood neprilysin levels are low in carriers, which is why the enzyme doubles as a biomarker. Notably, the reduction was described as mild in sural nerve in one series while enzymatic activity was significantly impaired, so the deficit is better characterised as catalytic than as a simple absence of protein.

nodes.description:
Foot orthoses for foot drop, and walking aids where balance is impaired. This is the only management with direct CMT2T evidence behind it: a genotyped patient whose walking impairment, foot drops and frequent falls improved with a foot orthosis, and several others in the same cohort recorded as using plantar orthoses, one with a cane.
Curated because the entry previously stated that CMT2T has no treatment while already quoting orthosis use in a phenotype description - the absence was an inconsistency, not a finding. It is supportive and compensatory: it does not modify the neuropathy, and nothing here should be read as suggesting it does.

nodes.description:
A single but clinically consequential observation. A homozygous MME patient with AR-CMT2T developed electrophysiological demyelinating changes and a biopsy showing endoneurial oedema with thinly myelinated fibres unevenly distributed within and between fascicles - a pattern that is inflammatory rather than genetic - and improved rapidly on immunoglobulin. The reporting authors propose that neprilysin loss makes the myelin sheath fragile and thereby triggers an immune response against peripheral myelin.
Curated despite resting on one patient because it changes management: an MME-positive patient whose course accelerates or whose conduction slows may have a treatable superimposed neuropathy, and the alternative reading - attributing the deterioration to the genetic disease - forecloses that. It is HYPOTHETICAL, and the proposed mechanism is the authors' own hypothesis, not a demonstrated one.
